docs.title: Smart Support Assistant API Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the Smart Support Assistant API Documentation.

This documentation provides complete reference material for integrating with the Zendesk-based Smart Support Assistant platform.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Smart Support Assistant is an AI-powered support automation system built using Zendesk APIs.

It enables applications to:

  • Create and manage support tickets
  • Retrieve ticket information
  • Manage users and organizations
  • Search support data
  • Automate support workflows
  • Generate AI-assisted responses
  • Improve customer support operations using AI workflows

docs.title: API Base URL
docs.text:
All API requests should be sent to the following base URL:

https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2

Example API request:

GET https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The Smart Support Assistant API uses Zendesk API authentication.

Supported authentication methods:

  • API Token Authentication
  • Basic Authentication

All API requests require authentication headers.

Example:

Authorization: Basic <encoded_credentials>
Content-Type: application/json

For detailed authentication information, refer to:

Authentication Guide

docs.title: API Modules
docs.text:
The API documentation is organized into the following modules:

Module Description Authentication API authentication and verification Tickets Create, retrieve, update, delete and manage support tickets Users User management operations Organizations Organization management operations Search Search tickets, users and organizations Views Manage Zendesk views Macros Manage and execute predefined actions Triggers Manage automation triggers AI Workflow AI-powered ticket analysis and response workflow Utilities Health checks, rate limits and error examples

docs.title: Get Tickets
docs.text:
Example request:

curl --request GET \
https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json \
--header "Authorization: Basic <token>" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json"

Example response:

{
  "tickets": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "subject": "Sample Support Ticket",
      "status": "open"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Smart Support Assistant uses Zendesk APIs to retrieve historical support information and assist users with accurate responses. Instead of directly answering a user's question, the AI searches for relevant support tickets, retrieves ticket details and comments, analyzes the information, and generates a response based on previous resolutions.

docs.title: AI Workflow Diagram
docs.text: The following diagram illustrates the AI-powered workflow used by the Smart Support Assistant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Search Zendesk for tickets that are relevant to the user's question.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• User question
  • Keywords extracted from the question

docs.title: API Used
docs.text: GET /api/v2/search.json?query={search_query}

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Matching ticket IDs
  • Ticket subjects
  • Basic ticket information

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Retrieve complete information for each relevant ticket.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: • Ticket ID

docs.title: API Used
docs.text: GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}.json

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Ticket Subject
  • Description
  • Status
  • Priority
  • Requester
  • Assignee
  • Tags
  • Created Date
  • Updated Date

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Retrieve the conversation history of the selected ticket.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: • Ticket ID

docs.title: API Used
docs.text: GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/comments.json

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Customer comments
  • Agent replies
  • Resolution steps
  • Troubleshooting information

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Generate a helpful response using the collected ticket information.

docs.title: AI Process
docs.text:
1. Read ticket details.
  2. Read ticket comments.
  3. Understand the issue.
  4. Identify previous successful resolutions.
  5. Generate a clear response for the user.

docs.title: Final Output
docs.text: A natural-language response based on historical Zendesk support data.

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["User Question:<br/>How can I reset my password?"]
    --> B["Search Relevant Tickets"]
    --> C["Find Matching Tickets"]
    --> D["Retrieve Ticket Details"]
    --> E["Retrieve Ticket Information"]
    --> F["Retrieve Ticket Comments"]
    --> G["Read Previous Conversation<br/>and Resolution"]
    --> H["AI Analysis"]
    --> I["Generate Response Based on<br/>Previous Successful Resolutions"]
    --> J["Final Response:<br/>1. Open the login page.<br/>2. Click 'Forgot Password'.<br/>3. Enter your registered email address.<br/>4. Open the password reset email.<br/>5. Create a new password."]

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Scenario Action No matching tickets found Inform the user that no relevant tickets were found. Ticket not accessible Skip the ticket and continue with other matching tickets. Authentication failure Return authentication error and stop the workflow. API rate limit exceeded Wait and retry the request after the specified interval. Network failure Retry the request or notify the user of the failure.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Search for relevant tickets before retrieving ticket details.
  • Retrieve comments only for relevant tickets.
  • Handle API errors gracefully.
  • Respect Zendesk API rate limits.
  • Avoid exposing sensitive customer information.
  • Use resolved tickets to improve response accuracy.
  • Log API requests and responses for troubleshooting.
  • Keep the workflow modular for future enhancements.

docs.title: Workflow Summary
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["User Question<br/>How can I reset my password?"]
    --> B["Search Relevant Tickets"]

    B --> C["Find Matching Tickets"]

    C --> D["Retrieve Ticket Details"]

    D --> E["Retrieve Ticket Comments"]

    E --> F["Analyze Ticket Details and Previous Resolutions"]

    F --> G["Generate AI Response"]

    G --> H["Final Response<br/><br/>1. Open the login page.<br/>2. Click 'Forgot Password'.<br/>3. Enter your registered email address.<br/>4. Open the password reset email.<br/>5. Create a new password."]

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Smart Support Assistant API uses the Zendesk REST API to manage customer support resources. Each API endpoint performs a specific operation such as creating tickets, managing users, searching records, or configuring automation.

The API enables applications to manage customer support operations including:

  • Ticket management
  • User management
  • Organization management
  • Search operations
  • Views and automation
  • AI-assisted ticket workflows

Each API endpoint performs a specific operation such as creating tickets, retrieving data, updating records, searching resources, or executing workflows.

docs.title: Zendesk Environment
docs.text:
Property Value Platform Zendesk REST API Zendesk Domain https://own-48441.zendesk.com API Version v2 Base URL https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2

This document provides an overview of the available API categories. Detailed documentation for each category is available in the docs/APIs folder.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Smart Support Assistant uses the Zendesk REST API for all operations. Every API request must be authenticated using a Zendesk API Token.

Authentication ensures that only authorized users can access and manage support resources.

docs.title: Zendesk Environment
docs.text: Property Value Zendesk Domain https://own-48441.zendesk.com API Base URL https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2 Authentication Type Basic Authentication with API Token

docs.title:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Zendesk API

    Client->>Zendesk API: API Request + API Token
    Zendesk API->>Zendesk API: Validate Credentials
    Zendesk API-->>Client: API Response
Authentication Method
docs.text:
Zendesk supports multiple authentication methods. This project uses:

  • Basic Authentication with API Token

The credentials consist of:

  • Zendesk Email Address
  • API Token

docs.title: Authentication Format
docs.text:
The username must include /token after your email address.

Email: your-email@example.com/token
Password: your_api_token

These credentials are Base64 encoded and sent in the Authorization header.

docs.title: Required HTTP Headers
docs.text:
Every API request should include the following headers:

Header Value Authorization Basic Base64(email/token:api_token) Content-Type application/json Accept application/json

docs.title: Example HTTP Request
docs.text:
GET /api/v2/tickets.json HTTP/1.1
Host: your-subdomain.zendesk.com
Authorization: Basic <Base64EncodedCredentials>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

docs.title: Using Postman
docs.text:
To authenticate in Postman:

  1. Open your request.
  2. Select the Authorization tab.
  3. Set Type to Basic Auth.

  4. Enter:

  5. Username: your-email@example.com/token

  6. Password: your_api_token
  7. Postman automatically generates the Authorization header.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
Follow these recommendations to keep your API credentials secure:

  • Never commit API tokens to Git repositories.
  • Store credentials in Postman Environments.
  • Use environment variables instead of hardcoding values.
  • Regenerate API tokens if they are exposed.
  • Grant only the minimum required permissions.

docs.title: Common Authentication Errors
docs.text: HTTP Status Code Description 401 Unauthorized Invalid email address or API token. 403 Forbidden The authenticated user does not have permission to perform the requested action.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: After authentication is configured, proceed to the API Overview to understand the available API categories and endpoints.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Macros in Zendesk are predefined sets of actions that agents can apply to tickets. These APIs allow you to:

  • List available macros
  • Retrieve a macro by ID
  • Apply a macro to a ticket

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: These APIs use Basic Authentication with a Zendesk API Token.

docs.title: Username
docs.text: your_email/token

docs.title: Password
docs.text: your_api_token

docs.title: Required Headers
docs.text: Header Value Authorization Basic Authentication Content-Type application/json Accept application/json

docs.title: 1. List Macros
docs.text: Retrieves all active macros available in the Zendesk account.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: GET /api/v2/macros.json

docs.title: Full URL
docs.text: https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2/macros.json

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Authorization Yes Content-Type application/json

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
GET /api/v2/macros.json HTTP/1.1
Host: own-48441.zendesk.com
Authorization: Basic <Base64EncodedCredentials>
Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
  "macros": [
    {
      "id": 28471046373404,
      "title": "Close and redirect to topics",
      "active": true
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text: Status Code Description 200 OK Macros retrieved successfully

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: Status Code Description 401 Unauthorized Invalid authentication credentials 403 Forbidden Access denied 404 Not Found Resource not found

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Returns all active macros.
  • Each macro includes its ID, title, and status.

docs.title: 2. Get Macro
docs.text: Retrieves detailed information about a specific macro.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: GET /api/v2/macros/{macro_id}.json

docs.title: Full URL
docs.text: https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2/macros/28471046373404.json

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description macro_id Integer Unique Macro ID

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Authorization Yes Content-Type application/json

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
GET /api/v2/macros/28471046373404.json HTTP/1.1
Host: own-48441.zendesk.com
Authorization: Basic <Base64EncodedCredentials>
Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
  "macro": {
    "id": 28471046373404,
    "title": "Close and redirect to topics",
    "active": true,
    "created_at": "2026-06-26T10:09:32Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-26T10:09:32Z"
  }
}

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text: Status Code Description 200 OK Macro retrieved successfully

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: Status Code Description 401 Unauthorized Invalid authentication credentials 404 Not Found Macro not found

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • Returns complete information for the specified macro.

docs.title: 3. Apply Macro
docs.text: Applies a macro to an existing ticket.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: PUT /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}.json?macro_id={macro_id}

docs.title: Full URL
docs.text: https://own-48441.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/1.json?macro_id=28471046373404

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description ticket_id Integer Ticket ID

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description macro_id Integer Macro ID to apply

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Authorization Yes Content-Type application/json

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: {}

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
PUT /api/v2/tickets/1.json?macro_id=28471046373404 HTTP/1.1
Host: own-48441.zendesk.com
Authorization: Basic <Base64EncodedCredentials>
Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
  "ticket": {
    "id": 1,
    "status": "closed"
  }
}

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text: Status Code Description 200 OK Macro applied successfully

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: Status Code Description 401 Unauthorized Invalid authentication credentials 404 Not Found Ticket or Macro not found 422 Unprocessable Entity Invalid request

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Applying a macro may automatically update:

  • Ticket status
  • Priority
  • Assignee
  • Tags
  • Custom fields
  • Internal/Public comments

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: API HTTP Method Description List Macros GET Retrieve all active macros Get Macro GET Retrieve a macro by ID Apply Macro PUT Apply a macro to a ticket

docs.title: Ticket Lifecycle
docs.text:
The following diagram illustrates the lifecycle of a support ticket in the Smart Support Assistant and Zendesk.

The ticket progresses through the following stages:

  1. Ticket Created
  2. Open
  3. Assigned
  4. In Progress
  5. Pending (if waiting for customer or external input)
  6. Solved
  7. Closed

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Smart Support Assistant follows a REST-based client-server architecture. It acts as an intermediary between client applications and the Zendesk REST API. The assistant receives requests from clients, validates authentication, forwards the requests to Zendesk, and returns the responses.

This architecture provides a secure, scalable, and maintainable way to integrate with Zendesk services.

docs.title: Architecture Diagram
docs.text: The following diagram illustrates the high-level architecture of the Smart Support Assistant.

docs.title: Client Application
docs.text: The client application sends HTTP requests to the Smart Support Assistant. It can be a web application, mobile application, or another backend service.

docs.title: Smart Support Assistant
docs.text: This component acts as the central processing layer. It performs authentication, validates requests, communicates with the Zendesk REST API, and returns responses to the client.

docs.title: Zendesk REST API
docs.text: The Zendesk REST API exposes endpoints for managing support resources such as tickets, users, organizations, views, macros, and triggers.

docs.title: Zendesk Platform
docs.text: The Zendesk platform stores customer support data and executes the requested operations before returning responses.

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
The request flow is as follows:

  1. The client application sends an HTTP request.
  2. The Smart Support Assistant validates the request.
  3. Authentication credentials are verified.
  4. The request is forwarded to the Zendesk REST API.
  5. Zendesk processes the request.
  6. A response is returned to the Smart Support Assistant.
  7. The Smart Support Assistant returns the response to the client.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
The architecture is designed with the following principles:

  • RESTful communication
  • Secure authentication
  • Modular design
  • Scalability
  • Maintainability
  • Reusability
  • Clear separation of responsibilities

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
This architecture offers several benefits:

  • Easy integration with Zendesk APIs.
  • Simplified API communication.
  • Centralized authentication.
  • Improved maintainability.
  • Better scalability for future enhancements.
  • Support for AI-assisted workflows.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: The next document explains how authentication works using Zendesk API Tokens and how to securely access the Smart Support Assistant APIs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document provides recommended practices for using the Smart Support Assistant and Zendesk APIs efficiently, securely, and reliably. Following these practices helps improve application performance, maintainability, and user experience.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Store API tokens securely.
  • Never hardcode API credentials in source code.
  • Use environment variables for sensitive information.
  • Rotate API tokens periodically.
  • Grant only the required permissions to API users.

docs.title: API Requests
docs.text:
• Use the correct HTTP method for each endpoint.
  • Validate request parameters before sending requests.
  • Use environment variables for the base URL and authentication details.
  • Avoid sending duplicate or unnecessary API requests.
  • Keep request payloads as small as possible.

docs.title: API Responses
docs.text:
• Always verify the HTTP status code.
  • Validate the response before processing data.
  • Handle empty or missing responses gracefully.
  • Log unexpected responses for troubleshooting.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Handle common HTTP errors such as 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, and 500.
  • Display meaningful error messages to users.
  • Retry requests only for temporary failures.
  • Log detailed error information for debugging.

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
• Monitor the remaining API request limit.
  • Respect the Retry-After response header.
  • Avoid sending requests in rapid succession.
  • Implement retry logic with delays when necessary.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Retrieve only the required data.
  • Cache frequently used information whenever possible.
  • Minimize the number of API calls.
  • Reuse existing API responses instead of making duplicate requests.
  • Execute requests in an efficient order.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Use HTTPS for all API communication.
  • Protect API tokens and user credentials.
  • Avoid exposing sensitive customer information.
  • Restrict access based on user permissions.
  • Remove sensitive data from logs whenever possible.

docs.title: AI Workflow
docs.text:
For the Smart Support Assistant, follow this sequence:

  1. Search relevant tickets.
  2. Retrieve ticket details.
  3. Retrieve ticket comments.
  4. Analyze the collected information.
  5. Generate the AI response.

This approach reduces unnecessary API calls and improves response quality.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Test each API endpoint individually.
  • Verify successful and failed responses.
  • Test authentication failures.
  • Test invalid request parameters.
  • Test rate limit handling.
  • Verify JSON response formats.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Keep API documentation up to date.
  • Document all endpoints clearly.
  • Include example requests and responses.
  • Record changes in the changelog.
  • Review documentation regularly.

docs.title: Logging and Monitoring
docs.text:
• Log API requests and responses.
  • Monitor API performance.
  • Track failed requests.
  • Record unexpected errors.
  • Review logs periodically to identify recurring issues.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Following these best practices helps ensure that the Smart Support Assistant is secure, reliable, and efficient. Proper authentication, structured API usage, effective error handling, rate limit awareness, and regular testing contribute to a stable and maintainable integration with the Zendesk API.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document describes the common errors that may occur while using the Smart Support Assistant APIs and explains how to identify and handle them.

Proper error handling helps applications provide meaningful feedback to users and improves system reliability.

docs.title: Error Response Format
docs.text:
When an API request fails, Zendesk returns an HTTP status code along with a JSON response containing details about the error.

Example:

{
  "error": "RecordNotFound",
  "description": "Not found"
}

docs.title: Common HTTP Status Codes
docs.text: Status Code Meaning Description 200 OK The request completed successfully. 201 Created A new resource was created successfully. 400 Bad Request The request contains invalid or missing data. 401 Unauthorized Authentication failed due to invalid credentials. 403 Forbidden Access to the requested resource is denied. 404 Not Found The requested resource does not exist. 409 Conflict The request conflicts with an existing resource. 422 Unprocessable Entity Validation failed for the submitted data. 429 Too Many Requests API rate limit has been exceeded. 500 Internal Server Error An unexpected server error occurred. 503 Service Unavailable The service is temporarily unavailable.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The request contains invalid parameters or malformed data.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Verify all required parameters.
  • Check the request body format.
  • Ensure the endpoint URL is correct.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: Authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Verify your Zendesk email address.
  • Verify your API token.
  • Ensure Basic Authentication is configured correctly.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The authenticated user does not have permission to access the requested resource.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Verify the user's permissions.
  • Ensure the account has access to the requested API.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The requested resource does not exist.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Verify the Ticket ID.
  • Verify the endpoint URL.
  • Ensure the resource has not been deleted.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The requested operation conflicts with the current state of the resource.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Review the existing resource.
  • Retry the request after resolving the conflict.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The request data failed validation.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Verify required fields.
  • Check field values and formats.
  • Correct validation errors before retrying.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: Too many requests were sent within a short period.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Wait before sending additional requests.
  • Reduce the request frequency.
  • Implement retry logic with delays.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: An unexpected server error occurred.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Retry the request after some time.
  • If the problem continues, contact Zendesk support.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The Zendesk service is temporarily unavailable.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Wait and retry the request later.
  • Monitor the Zendesk service status.

docs.title: Best Practices for Error Handling
docs.text:
• Always check the HTTP status code.
  • Read the error message returned by the API.
  • Validate request data before sending requests.
  • Handle authentication failures gracefully.
  • Implement retry logic for temporary failures.
  • Log API errors for troubleshooting.
  • Display user-friendly error messages instead of raw API responses.

docs.title: Example Error Handling Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Send API Request"]
    --> B["Receive Response"]

    B --> C{"Is Status Code 2xx?"}

    C -->|Yes| D["Process Data"]
    D --> E["Continue Workflow"]

    C -->|No| F["Read Error Response"]

    F --> G["Determine Cause"]

    G --> H["Apply Appropriate Solution"]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Proper error handling improves the reliability of the Smart Support Assistant by detecting API failures, providing meaningful error messages, and enabling the application to recover gracefully whenever possible.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Zendesk enforces API rate limits to ensure fair usage and maintain system performance. If an application sends too many requests within a short period, the API temporarily rejects additional requests until the limit resets.

This guide explains how rate limits work and how to handle them in the Smart Support Assistant.

docs.title: Why Rate Limits Exist
docs.text:
Rate limits help to:

  • Prevent server overload
  • Ensure fair usage among all users
  • Protect API performance
  • Improve system stability

docs.title: How Rate Limiting Works
docs.text:
Each API request counts toward your account's request limit.

When the limit is reached:

  • Zendesk returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response.
  • Additional requests are rejected until the rate limit resets.

docs.title: Rate Limit Response
docs.text:
When the rate limit is exceeded, the API returns:

Status Code Description 429 Too Many Requests

Example response:

{
  "error": "RateLimitExceeded",
  "description": "Rate limit exceeded. Please retry later."
}

docs.title: Rate Limit Headers
docs.text:
Zendesk includes response headers that provide information about the current rate limit.

Header Description X-Rate-Limit Maximum requests allowed X-Rate-Limit-Remaining Remaining requests available Retry-After Number of seconds to wait before retrying

Example:

X-Rate-Limit: 700
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 695
Retry-After: 30

docs.title: Handling Rate Limits
docs.text:
When a 429 Too Many Requests response is received:

  1. Stop sending additional requests.
  2. Read the Retry-After header.
  3. Wait for the specified number of seconds.
  4. Retry the request.
  5. Continue normal processing.

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Send API Request"]
    --> B["Receive Response"]

    B --> C{"Is Status Code 429?"}

    C -->|No| D["Continue Workflow"]

    C -->|Yes| E["Read Retry-After Header"]

    E --> F["Wait Specified Time"]

    F --> G["Retry the Request"]

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Avoid sending unnecessary API requests.
  • Cache frequently used data whenever possible.
  • Combine requests when appropriate.
  • Monitor the remaining request count.
  • Respect the Retry-After header.
  • Implement automatic retry logic with delays.
  • Avoid sending multiple simultaneous requests when possible.

docs.title: Recommendations for Smart Support Assistant
docs.text:
To improve performance and reduce the chance of hitting rate limits:

  • Search for relevant tickets before requesting ticket details.
  • Retrieve comments only for selected tickets.
  • Reuse previously retrieved data whenever possible.
  • Minimize duplicate API calls.
  • Handle rate limit responses gracefully.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Zendesk API rate limits help maintain reliable service for all users. The Smart Support Assistant should monitor rate limit headers, avoid excessive requests, and automatically retry requests after the recommended waiting period to ensure smooth and reliable API communication.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Smart Support Assistant is a REST API-based application that integrates with the Zendesk platform to simplify customer support operations. It enables developers and support teams to create, update, search, and manage support resources through Zendesk APIs.

The system acts as a bridge between client applications and the Zendesk platform, providing a structured and secure way to access support-related data.

docs.title: System Components
docs.text: The Smart Support Assistant consists of the following components:

docs.title: 1. Client Application
docs.text: The client application is the interface used by end users or developers. It sends HTTP requests to perform operations such as creating tickets or retrieving user information.

docs.title: 2. Smart Support Assistant
docs.text: The Smart Support Assistant processes incoming requests, validates authentication, prepares API calls, and communicates with the Zendesk REST API.

docs.title: 3. Zendesk REST API
docs.text: The Zendesk REST API provides endpoints for managing tickets, users, organizations, views, macros, triggers, and other support resources.

docs.title: 4. Zendesk Platform
docs.text: The Zendesk platform stores and manages all customer support data and returns responses to API requests.

docs.title: System Workflow
docs.text:
The typical request flow is:

  1. The client application sends an HTTP request.
  2. The Smart Support Assistant validates the request and authentication.
  3. The Smart Support Assistant forwards the request to the Zendesk REST API.
  4. Zendesk processes the request and returns a response.
  5. The Smart Support Assistant sends the response back to the client application.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
The Smart Support Assistant provides the following capabilities:

  • Ticket Management
  • User Management
  • Organization Management
  • Search Operations
  • View Management
  • Macro Execution
  • Trigger Automation
  • AI-Assisted Workflow
  • Secure Authentication
  • Error Handling
  • API Rate Limit Management

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Using the Smart Support Assistant provides several advantages:

  • Simplifies Zendesk API integration.
  • Provides consistent API documentation.
  • Reduces development time.
  • Improves maintainability.
  • Supports automation and AI-assisted workflows.
  • Enhances developer productivity.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This section provides answers to common questions about the Smart Support Assistant API, Zendesk integration, and the AI workflow.

docs.title: What is the Smart Support Assistant?
docs.text: The Smart Support Assistant is a system that uses Zendesk APIs to retrieve support ticket data and generate AI-based responses to user queries.

docs.title: What APIs are used in this project?
docs.text:
The system primarily uses:

  • Search API (to find relevant tickets)
  • Tickets API (to retrieve ticket details)
  • Ticket Comments API (to get conversation history)
  • Users API (for user-related information)

docs.title: What is the main purpose of this system?
docs.text: The main purpose is to assist support teams by automatically analyzing past tickets and providing accurate, context-based responses using AI.

docs.title: How do I authenticate with Zendesk API?
docs.text:
Zendesk uses Basic Authentication with an API token.

Format:

email/token:APIToken

Example:

john@example.com/token:abc123xyz

docs.title: Where do I get my API token?
docs.text:
You can generate an API token from your Zendesk Admin settings under:

Admin Center → Apps and Integrations → APIs → Zendesk API

docs.title: What is a ticket?
docs.text: A ticket is a customer support request created in Zendesk.

docs.title: How do I search for tickets?
docs.text:
You can use the Search API:

GET /api/v2/search.json?query={keyword}

docs.title: How do I get ticket details?
docs.text:
Use the Ticket API:

GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}.json

docs.title: How do I get ticket comments?
docs.text:
Use the Comments API:

GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/comments.json

docs.title: What does 401 Unauthorized mean?
docs.text: It means your API credentials are incorrect or missing.

docs.title: What does 404 Not Found mean?
docs.text: It means the requested ticket or resource does not exist.

docs.title: What does 429 Too Many Requests mean?
docs.text: It means you have exceeded the API rate limit and must wait before sending more requests.

docs.title: What should I do if I hit a rate limit?
docs.text: Wait for the time specified in the Retry-After header before retrying the request.

docs.title: Can I avoid rate limits?
docs.text:
Yes, by:

  • Reducing unnecessary API calls
  • Caching responses
  • Sending requests efficiently

docs.title: How does the AI generate responses?
docs.text:
The AI:

  1. Searches relevant tickets
  2. Retrieves ticket details
  3. Fetches ticket comments
  4. Analyzes historical solutions
  5. Generates a response

docs.title: Does the AI store user data?
docs.text: No, the AI only uses available ticket data during processing and does not permanently store user information.

docs.title: Why is Postman used in this project?
docs.text:
Postman is used to:

  • Test Zendesk APIs
  • Validate responses
  • Simulate the AI workflow
  • Debug API issues

docs.title: Can I automate the API calls?
docs.text:
Yes, Postman collections can be automated using:

  • Collection Runner
  • Newman (CLI tool)

docs.title: Is my API token safe?
docs.text:
Yes, if you:

  • Do not share it publicly
  • Store it in environment variables
  • Avoid hardcoding it in code

docs.title: Is HTTPS required?
docs.text: Yes, all Zendesk API calls must use HTTPS for secure communication.

docs.title: API is not returning data. What should I do?
docs.text:
Check:

  • Authentication credentials
  • Endpoint URL
  • Ticket ID or query parameters

docs.title: Why am I getting empty search results?
docs.text:
Possible reasons:

  • Incorrect search query
  • No matching tickets exist
  • Filters are too strict

docs.text: This FAQ provides quick answers to common issues and questions related to the Smart Support Assistant API. It helps developers and users understand authentication, API usage, errors, and AI workflow behavior.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This glossary provides definitions of key terms used in the Smart Support Assistant API documentation. It helps readers understand technical concepts used across Zendesk APIs and the AI workflow.

docs.title: API (Application Programming Interface)
docs.text: A set of rules that allows different software systems to communicate with each other.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The process of verifying the identity of a user or system before allowing access to the API.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
The main URL used to access Zendesk APIs.

Example: 

https://own-48441.zendesk.com

docs.title: Comments (Ticket Comments)
docs.text: Messages exchanged between customers and support agents within a ticket.

docs.title: Client
docs.text: An application or system that sends requests to the Zendesk API.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: A structured guide that explains how APIs, systems, or workflows work.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
A specific URL where an API can be accessed.

Example: 

GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}.json

docs.title: Filter
docs.text: A condition used to narrow down search results in API queries.

docs.title: HTTP Status Code
docs.text:
A numeric code returned by the server to indicate the result of an API request.

Example: - 200 OK - 404 Not Found - 429 Too Many Requests

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text: A secure version of HTTP used for encrypted communication between client and server.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text: The process of connecting different systems or services to work together.

docs.title: Macro
docs.text: A predefined set of actions in Zendesk used to automate repetitive support tasks.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text: A software layer that processes requests between client and server.

docs.title: Postman
docs.text: A tool used for testing and documenting APIs.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text: The data sent in an API request body.

docs.title: Rate Limit
docs.text: A restriction that limits the number of API requests that can be made in a specific time period.

docs.title: Request
docs.text: A call made by a client to an API endpoint to perform an operation or retrieve data.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: The data returned by an API after processing a request.

docs.title: Search API
docs.text: An API used to find tickets, users, or other resources based on query parameters.

docs.title: Subdomain
docs.text:
The unique Zendesk domain assigned to an account.

Example: 

own-48441.zendesk.com

docs.title: Ticket
docs.text: A support request created by a customer in Zendesk.

docs.title: Token
docs.text: A secure key used for API authentication instead of a password.

docs.title: User
docs.text: A person who interacts with the Zendesk system, either as a customer or agent.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: A sequence of steps followed to complete a process, such as the AI response generation flow.

docs.title: Zendesk
docs.text: A customer service platform used for managing support tickets and customer interactions.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: This glossary helps clarify important terms used throughout the Smart Support Assistant API documentation. It ensures consistency and improves understanding of API concepts and workflows.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
HTTP status codes indicate the outcome of an API request. They help developers determine whether a request was successful or identify the reason for a failure.

The Smart Support Assistant uses standard HTTP status codes returned by the Zendesk API.

docs.title: 200 OK
docs.text:
Description

The request was successful, and the server returned the requested data.

Example Usage

  • Search tickets
  • Get ticket details
  • Get ticket comments
  • Retrieve users
  • Retrieve organizations

docs.title: 201 Created
docs.text:
Description

The request was successful, and a new resource was created.

Example Usage

  • Create a new ticket
  • Create a user
  • Create an organization

docs.title: 204 No Content
docs.text:
Description

The request was successful, but there is no content to return.

Example Usage

  • Delete a resource
  • Update a resource without returning data

docs.title: 400 Bad Request
docs.text:
Description

The request contains invalid data or missing parameters.

Possible Causes

  • Invalid request body
  • Missing required field
  • Incorrect parameter

Recommended Action

Verify the request before sending it.

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
Description

Authentication failed.

Possible Causes

  • Invalid email
  • Invalid API token
  • Missing authentication

Recommended Action

Verify your authentication credentials.

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
Description

The authenticated user does not have permission to perform the requested operation.

Possible Causes

  • Insufficient permissions
  • Restricted resource

Recommended Action

Verify user permissions.

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
Description

The requested resource could not be found.

Possible Causes

  • Invalid Ticket ID
  • Invalid User ID
  • Incorrect endpoint

Recommended Action

Verify the resource identifier.

docs.title: 409 Conflict
docs.text:
Description

The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

Possible Causes

  • Duplicate operation
  • Resource conflict

Recommended Action

Review the existing resource before retrying.

docs.title: 422 Unprocessable Entity
docs.text:
Description

The request is valid, but the submitted data failed validation.

Possible Causes

  • Missing required fields
  • Invalid field values

Recommended Action

Correct the validation errors and resend the request.

docs.title: 429 Too Many Requests
docs.text:
Description

The API rate limit has been exceeded.

Possible Causes

  • Too many requests in a short period

Recommended Action

Wait for the duration specified in the Retry-After header before retrying.

docs.title: 500 Internal Server Error
docs.text:
Description

An unexpected error occurred on the server.

Recommended Action

Retry the request later.

docs.title: 502 Bad Gateway
docs.text:
Description

The server received an invalid response from an upstream service.

Recommended Action

Retry after a short delay.

docs.title: 503 Service Unavailable
docs.text:
Description

The service is temporarily unavailable.

Recommended Action

Wait and retry the request later.

docs.title: Status Code Summary
docs.text: Status Code Meaning Category 200 OK Success 201 Created Success 204 No Content Success 400 Bad Request Client Error 401 Unauthorized Client Error 403 Forbidden Client Error 404 Not Found Client Error 409 Conflict Client Error 422 Unprocessable Entity Client Error 429 Too Many Requests Client Error 500 Internal Server Error Server Error 502 Bad Gateway Server Error 503 Service Unavailable Server Error

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always check the HTTP status code before processing the response.
  • Handle both success and error responses appropriately.
  • Display user-friendly error messages.
  • Log unexpected errors for troubleshooting.
  • Implement retry logic for temporary server errors and rate limits.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Understanding HTTP status codes helps developers identify the outcome of API requests, troubleshoot issues efficiently, and build reliable integrations with the Zendesk API.
